name: Izere
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Lukas, Johannes & Willms, A. 1961. Outline of the Language of the Jarawa in Northern Nigeria (Plateau Province).
earlier_scan.note: Grammar sketch exists (also Blench Izere materials, but rogerblench.info domain is now squatted); no online copy reachable.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x reference list for izer1241 (16 refs) and Blench 2019 Atlas of Nigerian Languages ed. IV, entry 210 'Izere cluster'
sources.note: Bibliographic only; no further phonological descriptions listed beyond those above (Atlas: Survey Shimizu 1975, Regnier 1991; Dictionary Blench & Kaze).

sources.citation: Erin, Adewumi Anthony. 2022. A study of number marking in Izere nouns. Journal of Modern Languages 32(2): 84-106. doi:10.22452/jml.vol32no2.5
sources.note: Nothing on stress; treats Izere as a tone language with H, M, L and describes tonal plural marking. Its bibliography names Isha & Haruna 2016 'The syllable structure of Izere' (print festschrift chapter).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Bitrus Kaze. 2019. A dictionary of the Izere language of Fobur. 2019 edition. Jos/Cambridge: circulated electronic ms., 148 pp. (section 4 'The sound-system of Ibor Izere and the official orthography', pp. 10-11)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 4.1 gives 29 consonants, 7 vowels, 'three level and two contour tones (LM & HL)', tone-marking conventions; no mention of stress, accent (other than tone diacritics) or prominence anywhere in the 148 pp. (full-text searched).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Bitrus Kaze. n.d. [c. 2016]. Izere dictionary: introduction (earlier 20-page draft of the same front matter).
sources.note: Nothing; same phonology text as the 2019 edition (tones only).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2000. Transitions in Izere nominal morphology and implications for the analysis of Plateau languages. In A. Meissner & A. Storch (eds.), Nominal classification in African languages (Frankfurter Afrikanistische Blaetter 12), 7-28. Koeln: Koeppe. (author's scan, 11 pp., no text layer; scanned at 300 dpi)
sources.note: Nothing. Brief phonology (consonants, vowels, five tones: three level + LM, HL contours) then noun-class prefix/stem-tone alternations; no stress/accent statement in the scanned text.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. Plural verb morphology in Fobur Izere. Draft electronic ms., 21 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Short phonology preamble (section 2): consonants, 7 vowels, 'five tones in Izere, three level and two contour tones... underlying three-height system'; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Grainger, P. n.d. Izere phonology. Electronic ms., Izere Language Project / NBTT, Jos (cited in Blench & Kaze 2019).

sources.note: The phonology write-up underlying the Izere orthography; Blench relies on it for the segment inventory; would contain any suprasegmental statement (tone vs stress) made by the Bible-translation team.

sources.citation: Isha, V. I. N. & A. Haruna. 2016. The syllable structure of Izere. In O.-M. Ndimele, M. Ahmad & H. M. Yakasai (eds.), Language, literature and culture in a multilingual society: a festschrift, vol. 2, 753-762. Port Harcourt: M & J Grand Orbit Communications.

sources.note: Only dedicated modern paper on Izere syllable/prosodic structure; Nigerian phonology papers of this type usually state whether the language has stress or only tone.
